scheme_name: Assistance of Concentrate Feed for Pregnant Animals (Scheduled Tribe Category)
description:
The Assistance of Concentrate Feed for Pregnant Animals scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India to support Scheduled Tribe communities engaged in animal husbandry.

This scheme was officially launched in the year 2017 under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide nutritional support to pregnant animals owned by Scheduled Tribe families.

The scheme aims to improve the health and productivity of livestock among tribal communities.

By providing concentrate feed, the government seeks to enhance the overall well-being of both the animals and the families that depend on them for their livelihood.

The specific target of the scheme is to cover approximately 1 lakh pregnant animals annually.

The scheme intends to ensure that these animals receive adequate nutrition during their gestation period.

This is crucial as proper nutrition can lead to healthier offspring and improved milk production.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme amounts to INR 1,500 per pregnant animal.

This amount is intended to cover the cost of concentrate feed for the duration of the pregnancy.

The assistance is provided directly to the beneficiaries through a cash transfer mechanism.

To be eligible for this scheme, applicants must belong to Scheduled Tribe communities.

The scheme is specifically targeted at individuals who own pregnant animals.

There is no specific age limit for applicants.

However, applicants must be engaged in animal husbandry as a primary source of livelihood.

Income criteria for eligibility are set at an annual income of less than INR 2 lakhs.

This ensures that the benefits reach the economically weaker sections of the Scheduled Tribe communities.

The application process for the scheme is straightforward.

Interested beneficiaries must approach the local office of the Department of Animal Husbandry.

They need to fill out an application form that is available at these offices.

The required documents include proof of Scheduled Tribe status.

Applicants must also provide proof of ownership of the pregnant animal.

This can be in the form of a sale deed or any official document that establishes ownership.

Additionally, applicants must submit an income certificate.

Once the application is submitted, it will be verified by the concerned authorities.

Verification typically takes about 15 to 30 days.

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the beneficiary's bank account.

The disbursement is usually done within a month of approval.

The scheme is implemented through the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

This department is responsible for overseeing the welfare of livestock in India.

The contact details for the Department of Animal Husbandry can be found on their official website.

State governments also play a crucial role in the implementation of this scheme.

They are responsible for the ground-level execution and monitoring of the program.

Regular audits and assessments are conducted to ensure that the benefits are reaching the intended beneficiaries.

The scheme has shown positive results in improving the health of pregnant animals.

It has also contributed to increasing the income levels of tribal families involved in animal husbandry.

As of 2023, it is estimated that over 50,000 pregnant animals have benefited from this scheme.

This has led to a significant increase in milk production in tribal areas.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the government to uplift Scheduled Tribe communities.

It aligns with the National Tribal Policy which aims to enhance the socio-economic conditions of tribal populations.

The government is committed to ensuring that tribal communities have access to resources and support.

This scheme is one of many that focus on sustainable livelihoods for tribal populations.

The nutritional support provided through this initiative is crucial for the development of the livestock sector.

It also plays a role in ensuring food security for tribal families.

The scheme has been well-received by the tribal communities.

Feedback from beneficiaries indicates a high level of satisfaction with the support provided.

The government continues to monitor the impact of the scheme on livestock health and productivity.

Regular workshops and training sessions are conducted to educate beneficiaries about animal husbandry practices.

These sessions focus on the importance of nutrition and proper care for pregnant animals.

The government also collaborates with NGOs and local organizations to enhance the outreach of the scheme.

This collaboration helps in identifying potential beneficiaries and ensuring that the assistance reaches those in need.

The Assistance of Concentrate Feed for Pregnant Animals scheme is a vital step towards empowering tribal communities.

It not only supports animal husbandry but also promotes sustainable agricultural practices.

The scheme is expected to evolve over the coming years.

Future enhancements may include increased financial assistance or additional support services.

The government is committed to continuously improving the welfare of Scheduled Tribe communities.

This scheme is a testament to that commitment.

It reflects the government's recognition of the importance of livestock in the livelihoods of tribal families.

Overall, the Assistance of Concentrate Feed for Pregnant Animals scheme is a significant initiative.

It aims to uplift the socio-economic status of Scheduled Tribe communities through targeted support in animal husbandry.

The scheme's focus on nutritional assistance is crucial for the health of both animals and their owners.

It represents a comprehensive approach to welfare that addresses both immediate needs and long-term sustainability.
